'''Suwa Gorōnin''' (諏訪御料人, 1530 – December 18, 1555) was a concubine of {{ill|Takeda Shingen|ar|تاكيدا شين-غن|az|Takeda Şingen|ban|Takeda Shingen|ca|Takeda Shingen|cs|Šingen Takeda|de|Takeda Shingen|eo|Takeda Shingen|es|Takeda Shingen|fa|تاکدا شینگن|fi|Takeda Shingen|fr|Takeda Shingen|hak|Takeda Shingen|he|טקדה שינגן|hu|Takeda Singen|id|Takeda Shingen|it|Takeda Shingen|ja|武田信玄|jv|Takeda Shingen|ko|다케다 신겐|nl|Takeda Shingen|no|Takeda Shingen|pl|Shingen Takeda|pt|Takeda Shingen|ru|Такэда Сингэн|sk|Šingen Takeda|sq|Takeda Shingen|sr|Такеда Шинген|sv|Takeda Shingen|th|ทาเกดะ ชิงเง็ง|tr|Takeda Shingen|uk|Такеда Шінґен|vi|Takeda Shingen|wuu|武田信玄|zh|武田信玄|zh_min_nan|Takeda Singen|zh_yue|武田信玄|zu|Takeda Shingen|qid=Q276404|lt=Takeda Shingen}}{{efn|Japanese feudal lord (1521–1573)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takeda Shingen|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Takeda Harunobu) and the mother of {{ill|Takeda Katsuyori|ar|تاكيدا كاتسويوري|cs|Kacujori Takeda|de|Takeda Katsuyori|eo|Takeda Katsuyori|es|Takeda Katsuyori|eu|Takeda Katsuyori|fa|تاکدا کاتسویوری|fr|Takeda Katsuyori|id|Takeda Katsuyori|it|Takeda Katsuyori|ja|武田勝頼|ko|다케다 가쓰요리|ms|Takeda Katsuyori|nl|Takeda Katsuyori|pl|Katsuyori Takeda|pt|Takeda Katsuyori|ro|Takeda Katsuyori|ru|Такэда Кацуёри|sr|Такеда Кацујори|th|ทาเกดะ คัตสึโยริ|tr|Takeda Katsuyori|uk|Такеда Кацуйорі|zh|武田勝賴|zh_min_nan|Takeda Katuyori|qid=Q662482|lt=Takeda Katsuyori}}. She was the daughter of {{ill|Suwa Yorishige|ja|諏訪頼重|ko|스와 요리시게|nl|Suwa Yorishige|qid=Q1213900|lt=Suwa Yorishige}}, the head of the {{ill|Suwa clan|de|Suwa (Klan)|fa|خاندان سووا|fr|Clan Suwa|id|Klan Suwa|it|Clan Suwa|ja|諏訪氏|ko|스와씨|pt|Clã Suwa|ru|Сува (род)|qid=Q2975376|lt=Suwa clan}}, and his concubine from the {{ill|Omi clan (麻績氏)|ja|小見氏|qid=Q11463661}} (Omishi). Known also as "Taikata-sama," her actual name remains unknown. In historical sources, she is referred to as "Suwa Gorōnin" or "Suwa Gozen," both terms indicating a noblewoman.

== Biography ==
Suwa Gorōnin's birth year is uncertain, but according to the ''{{ill|Kōyō Gunkan|es|Kōyō Gunkan|fa|کویو گونکان|fr|Kōyō gunkan|it|Kōyō Gunkan|ja|甲陽軍鑑|ko|고요군칸|zh|甲陽軍鑑|qid=Q586111|lt=Kōyō Gunkan}}'', she became a concubine of Takeda Shingen at age 14 in 1545, suggesting she was born in 1530.<ref name="hira23">{{Cite book|author=平山優|title=長篠合戦と武田勝頼 敗者の日本史9|publisher=吉川弘文館|year=2014|page=23}}</ref><ref name="shiba476">{{Cite book|author=柴辻俊六|title=武田氏家臣団人名辞典|publisher=東京堂出版|year=2015|page=476}}</ref> ''Kōyō Gunkan'' praises her beauty, calling her a "notable beauty."<ref name="shiba476" />

At the time of her father Suwa Yorishige's leadership, the Suwa clan was allied with the {{ill|Takeda clan|ar|عشيرة تاكيدا|ca|Clan Takeda|cs|Klan Takeda|de|Takeda (Klan)|eo|Takeda (klano)|es|Clan Takeda|eu|Takeda klana|fa|خاندان تاکدا|fr|Clan Takeda|glk|تاكدا كوگا|hu|Takeda-ház|id|Klan Takeda|it|Clan Takeda|ja|武田氏|ko|다케다씨|mk|Такеда (клан)|nl|Takeda (familie)|no|Takeda-klanen|pl|Takeda (ród)|pt|Clã Takeda|ru|Такэда|sr|Клан Такеда|th|ตระกูลทาเกดะ|tr|Takeda boyu|uk|Рід Такеда|zh|武田氏|qid=Q1210114|lt=Takeda clan}}. Yorishige married {{ill|Nene Goryōnin|fa|ننه گوریونین|ja|禰々|zh|武田禰禰|qid=Q11124807|lt=Neene}}, Takeda Shingen's half-sister, to strengthen the alliance. However, in 1541, after Shingen ousted his father {{ill|Takeda Nobutora|de|Takeda Nobutora|fa|تاکدا نوبوتورا|fr|Takeda Nobutora|it|Takeda Nobutora|ja|武田信虎|kk|Тэкада Нобутара|ko|다케다 노부토라|nl|Takeda Nobutora|no|Takeda Nobutora|ru|Такэда Нобутора|tr|Takeda Nobutora|uk|Такеда Нобутора|wuu|武田信虎|zh|武田信虎|qid=Q1192628|lt=Takeda Nobutora}}, Yorishige aligned with the {{ill|Uesugi clan|ca|Clan Uesugi|de|Uesugi|es|Clan Uesugi|eu|Uesugi klana|fa|خاندان اوئه‌سوگی|fr|Clan Uesugi|it|Clan Uesugi|ja|上杉氏|ko|우에스기씨|ms|Puak Uesugi|pl|Uesugi (ród)|pt|Clã Uesugi|ru|Уэсуги (род)|th|ตระกูลอูเอซูงิ|tr|Uesugi boyu|uk|Рід Уесуґі|vi|Gia tộc Uesugi|zh|上杉氏|qid=Q1150058|lt=Uesugi clan}}, violating the Takeda-Suwa alliance. This led to Takeda's invasion of Suwa, resulting in the fall of the Suwa clan and Yorishige's forced seppuku.

To consolidate his control, Shingen took Suwa Gorōnin as a concubine and planned to have their son, Katsuyori, inherit the Suwa clan's legacy.<ref name="hira23" /> She is believed to have entered the Takeda household around 1545, residing at the {{ill|Tsutsujigasaki Castle|es|Castillo de Tsutsujigasaki|fa|قلعه تسوتسوجیگاساکی|fr|Château de Tsutsujigasaki|ja|躑躅ヶ崎館|ko|쓰쓰지가사키관|zh|躑躅崎館|qid=Q11637200|lt=Tsutsujigasaki Mansion}}.<ref name="shiba476" />

Suwa Gorōnin died on November 6, 1555. Her grave is located at {{ill|Kenpuku-ji|ja|建福寺|qid=Q20044158}} in present-day {{ill|Ina, Nagano|ar|إنا (ناغانو)|azb|اینا، ناقانو|ce|Ина (гӀала)|ceb|Ina (lungsod sa Hapon)|de|Ina (Nagano)|es|Ina (Nagano)|fa|اینا، ناگانو|fi|Ina (Nagano)|fr|Ina (Nagano)|gl|Ina|hy|Ինա (քաղաք)|id|Ina, Nagano|it|Ina (Nagano)|ja|伊那市|ko|이나시|mzn|اینا، ناگانو|nl|Ina (Nagano)|pl|Ina (miasto)|pt|Ina (Nagano)|ro|Ina|ru|Ина (город)|sv|Ina, Nagano|tg|Ина|th|อินะ|tl|Ina, Nagano|tr|Ina, Nagano|tt|Ина (шәһәр)|uk|Іна (Наґано)|ur|اینا، ناگانو|uz|Ina (Nagano)|vi|Ina, Nagano|war|Ina, Nagano|zh|伊那市|zh_classical|伊那市|zh_min_nan|Ina-chhī|zh_yue|伊那|qid=Q840888|lt=Ina, Nagano}}. Her Buddhist name was recorded as "Kenpukuji-dono Baigan Myōkō Daizenni."<ref name="shiba476" /> Another memorial exists at {{ill|Kannon-in (Okaya City)|ja|観音院 (岡谷市)|qid=Q11630661}} in {{ill|Okaya, Nagano|ar|أوكايا (ناغانو)|azb|اوکایا، ناقانو|ce|Окая|ceb|Okaya (lungsod sa Hapon)|de|Okaya|es|Okaya (Nagano)|fa|اوکایا|fi|Okaya|fr|Okaya (Nagano)|gl|Okaya|hy|Օկայա|id|Okaya, Nagano|it|Okaya|ja|岡谷市|ko|오카야시|mzn|اوکایا، ناگانو|nl|Okaya|no|Okaya|pl|Okaya|pt|Okaya|ro|Okaya|ru|Окая|sv|Okaya|tg|Окая|th|โอกายะ|tl|Okaya, Nagano|tr|Okaya|tt|Окая|uk|Окая (Наґано)|ur|اوکایا، ناگانو|uz|Okaya (Nagano)|vi|Okaya, Nagano|war|Okaya, Nagano|zh|岡谷市|zh_classical|岡谷市|zh_min_nan|Okaya-chhī|zh_yue|岡谷|qid=Q838672|lt=Okaya, Nagano}}, but it was constructed after her death based on fictional accounts.

== Influence and Legacy ==
According to ''{{ill|Tetsuzan-shū|ja|鉄山集}}'' and ''Butsugan Zenji Goroku,'' her son Katsuyori performed rituals in her memory, including the 17th death anniversary ceremony in 1571.<ref name="shiba476" />

There is speculation that she was adopted by {{ill|Netsu Motonao|ja|禰津元直|qid=Q11594497}} to avoid her identity as a former enemy's daughter. This adoption would mean Katsuyori and {{ill|Takeda Nobukiyo|fa|تاکدا نوبوکیو|ja|武田信清|zh|武田信清|qid=Q6639853}} were both her children, suggesting she lived until the 1560s.

== Cultural Impact ==
Suwa Gorōnin is often depicted as Takeda Shingen's favorite concubine, although this characterization is debated among historians. Historical dramas and novels have contributed to this portrayal, such as {{ill|Jirō Nitta|arz|چيرو نيتا|de|Nitta Jirō|fa|جیرو نیتتا|fr|Jirō Nitta|ja|新田次郎|qid=Q3179274|lt=Jirō Nitta}}'s ''{{ill|Takeda Shingen (novel)|ja|Takeda Shingen (小説)}}'', where she is called "Koi-hime," and {{ill|Yasushi Inoue|ar|ياسوشي اينو|arz|ياسوشى اينو|bg|Иноуе Ясуши|cs|Jasuši Inoue|de|Yasushi Inoue|el|Γιασούσι Ινουέ|eo|Yasushi Inoue|es|Yasushi Inoue|eu|Yasushi Inoue|fa|یاسوشی اینواوئه|fi|Yasushi Inoue|fr|Yasushi Inoue|hu|Inoue Jaszusi|hy|Յասուսի Ինոուե|it|Yasushi Inoue|ja|井上靖|ka|იასუში ინოუე|ko|이노우에 야스시|pl|Yasushi Inoue|pt|Yasushi Inoue|ro|Yasushi Inoue|ru|Иноуэ, Ясуси|sl|Jasuši Inoue|uk|Ясусі Іноуе|uz|Inoue, Yasushi|zh|井上靖|qid=Q712734|lt=Yasushi Inoue}}'s ''{{ill|The Samurai Banner of Furin Kazan|ja|風林火山 (小説)|zh|风林火山 (小说)|qid=Q11665512}}'', where she is named "Yūbu-hime." 

The annual {{ill|Shingen-ko Festival|de|Shingen-kō Matsuri|fa|جشنواره شینگن‌کو|ja|信玄公祭り|qid=Q3562464|lt=Shingen-kō Festival}} in {{ill|Kōfu|ar|كوفو (ياماناشي)|arz|كوفو|az|Kofu|azb|کوفو، یاماناشی|ban|Kōfu|be|Кофу (горад)|bg|Кофу|ca|Kōfu|ce|Кофу (гӀала)|ceb|Kōfu-shi (distrito)|cs|Kófu|de|Kōfu|eo|Kofu|es|Kōfu (Yamanashi)|et|Kōfu|eu|Kōfu|fa|کوفو (یاماناشی)|fi|Kōfu|fr|Kōfu|ga|Kōfu|gl|Kōfu, Yamanashi|he|קופו|hu|Kófu|hy|Կոֆու (քաղաք)|id|Kōfu, Yamanashi|it|Kōfu|ja|甲府市|ka|კოფუ|ko|고후시|lt|Kofu|mg|Kōfu|mt|Kōfu|mzn|کوفو، یاماناشی|nl|Kofu|no|Kōfu|pl|Kōfu|pt|Kōfu|ro|Kōfu, Yamanashi|ru|Кофу (город)|sc|Kōfu|sh|Kōfu|simple|Kōfu|sr|Кофу|su|Kofu, Yamanashi|sv|Kōfu|sw|Kofu, Yamanashi|szl|Kōfu|tg|Кофу|th|โคฟุ|tl|Kōfu, Yamanashi|tr|Kōfu|tt|Кофу (шәһәр)|tum|Kōfu|uk|Кофу (Яманасі)|ur|کوفو، یاماناشی|vi|Kōfu, Yamanashi|war|Kōfu, Yamanashi|wuu|甲府市|zh|甲府市|zh_classical|甲府市|zh_min_nan|Kôhu-chhī|zh_yue|甲府|qid=Q201932|lt=Kōfu, Yamanashi}} features a "Koi-hime Contest," adding to her legacy in popular culture.
